accuracy.why: Nothing of the sources is missing or added as a fact in the 161 strings (stage 4's fence; the independent proof re-read all of them), the palms figure is the source's in the ruled scale, and one approximation of round 1 is gone: cat.crafts.d no longer reads 'by local hands' with the date-picking. Two points off for what remains approximate: no brand in foot.independence and inline.home.title (N1); «سرگرمیاں» / «سرگرمی» narrower than 'experiences'; map.locate.err says 'give the permission' where the sources say 'check' it; home.name.body carries «عربی», which the sources leave unsaid (N7); list.empty says 'not found yet' for 'none yet'; nav.blog («مضامین») and nav.dining («کھانے پینے کی جگہیں») name the content where the source names the format.

nativeness.why: Up one, on a second reading. A reader who knew nothing of the first found no serious fault, passed fourteen of the nineteen round-1 edits without remark or with assent (the lakh figure, «مینو», «لنک کاپی ہو گیا ✓», «سیر کریں», «فاصلے اندازاً دیے گئے ہیں», the 404 line, of which he had 'nothing to report'), and called the translated images of the home page 'understood; taste only'. Five points off for what two readers still hear: those images («زندگی کا وعدہ کرتا ہے», «ورثے کا دل», «نخلستان کو محسوس کرنے», «روح سمیٹ لیتے ہیں», «آہنگ») and the brochure heading of home.plan.title; «داستان» five times; «سیاحتی رہنما» as a person; «راہ» and «راستہ» for two things; «مواد», «تقریبات», «ترشاوہ پھلوں»; and, on round-1 wordings that stay, «فارم» first read as a form, «دن میں» as no part of the day, «سیر مکمل کرنا», and «اشتراک کریں» where he expects the loan. Eight strings carry this round's edits and are unread, though each stands in a reader's or an earlier stage's words, or changes only an order, a mark or a spelling.

compliance.why: Up one. An independent proof read the round-1 text on the eleven items: no forbidden letterform and no non-Latin digit in 5031 code points, every name byte-identical («الاحساء» 16 times), every loan equal to an entry that cites P16, the agreements of the edits right («لنک کاپی ہو گیا», «اپنی سیر»); its one finding was in three termbase notes, rewritten here. The stage checker now reads the P10 ruling and reports nothing. This round's eight strings were scanned by this stage and their agreements re-read («یہیں کے لوگوں کے ہاتھوں چوغوں پر کڑھائی», «اجازت دے دیں», «“حسی” کی جمع ہے»). One point off: five entries stay pending («حسی», «مفلق», «بندرگاہ», «حساوی لیموں کا باغ», «براؤزر»), three genders follow usage against a printed label («بندرگاہ», «ریت», «کھجوریں»), and this round's edits await their own proof.

fit.why: Two readers on phones, the second with a phone set to Urdu: the palms in lakh without a remark («25 لاکھ+»), the menu, the copied-link message and the share verb recognised, the distance button and the not-found block clear; the location message now says what to do and keeps «مقام» for the places («براؤزر میں اس ویب سائٹ کو یہ جاننے کی اجازت دے دیں»). One point off for what the traveller still trips on that is the Urdu's to carry: «داستانوں» beside a mosque sat uneasily with both readers (home.route.s4.d); «قصر» and «سوق» stand unexplained in labels, one reader each; «حسی» has needed two rounds; and the site's own name appears only in Latin, with the code «UR» on the button.

blind_reader_rulings.reason: As the first reader (observation 4): 'Oasis Fruits' / «ثمار الواحة» does not say what the section holds in either source; the owner's navigation queue lists it. Two readers now.
As the first reader (observation 5): 'Online Stores' / «المتاجر» says neither whose shops nor that the page is a directory; that the footer has no such link is the site's structure. Two readers now.

On a round-1 wording, weighed as any stage's would be. The two readers disagree: the first could make nothing of «کھیت» ('nobody goes sightseeing to a crop field') and did not recover; the second read «فارم» first as a form to fill in and as farms on the second pass, and asks for «باغات». What has evidence beyond taste is «فارم»: the press calls these very farms so and it is a headword of Urdu Lughat. «باغات» is refused on two grounds: it would erase a distinction the Arabic makes («المنتزهات», «المزارع») — in this batch the word is the 'gardens' of the parks label, and the reader himself took that label for the farms group; and the group holds a rice farm, a strawberry farm and a zoo, none of which is a «باغ». No wording an earlier reader passed exists to return to. The first-pass reading is charged under nativeness, and the form that removes it, the press's own «زرعی فارم», is measured and on record (155.8px; beside «رہائش» the bar would need 1457px) for a third reader who stops there. That the farm's own name says «باغ» is for the round that writes its page (entry pending; proof note 3).

As the first reader (observations 2 and 17), and now twice: it is the sources that call the six subject cards 'paths' on the home page («اختر طريقك», «مساراتٌ تختصر لك الأحساء» — the Arabic even uses its word for the trails) and 'categories' on the index. One word for both, as he proposes, would erase what the Arabic keeps apart. That «سیر کے راستے» can be read as walking paths is true of 'Trails' as well.

As the first reader (observations 10 and 30): two tools and three names for planning, 'favourite' beside 'saved', and a 'starting point' that is never named, all in both sources; the owner's navigation queue carries the first. Two readers now.

The same remark and the same three words as the first reader (observation 6). Still refused, and now on record as a one-line option for the owner: «میلے اور تقریبات» puts into the label a word the source label does not carry ('Events', «الفعاليات»), in three strings that share one English, and as a bar label it fits only beside the shorter «رہائش» (measured: 83px against 41.8px; the bar would need 1470 of its 1478px). «تقریبات» is the dictionary's word, and both readers found «میلے» on the card under it at once.

Two readers, one word: «رہائش» in the bar and in the footer (changes nav.stayShort and nav.stay). Native for native, the same meaning, no ground against it, and it fits the bar with room to spare (need 1428px).

As the first reader (observation 12): «گائیڈ» is on the owner's banned list. He says the title and the disclaimer are clear; as a bare eyebrow over the list page the word stays what it is, and no other wording was offered by either reader. Charged under nativeness.

No wording was offered, and «مواد» is the word of Urdu sites for exactly these two links (BBC Urdu, DW, VOA). Round 1's edit is confirmed on its own point: with «اصل» gone he no longer reads 'the original material'. Both strings are an accessible name and a link that shows only on keyboard focus, and the page now marks them so.
The source lists 'sights' and 'places' side by side («معلم … مكان»), as the first reader also saw (observation 8). «سرگرمی», which round 1 put in the same field, drew no remark.
The footer column is headed 'Plan' and its first link is 'Plan your trip' in the English, and the Urdu repeats as the source does (stage 2 recorded it).

As the first reader (observation 33), and still refused: the Arabic makes the distinction («جهة حكومية», «هيئة رسمية») and a disclaimer says the thing twice on purpose. His sentence turns 'is not a government body' into 'is not a government website': a change in how the site states what it is, which is the owner's (P25). On record as a one-line option: «یہ کوئی سرکاری ویب سائٹ نہیں اور نہ کسی سرکاری ادارے کی نمائندگی کرتی ہے۔».

The brand line of /ur/ is the question ruling P2 left unanswered and this batch does not settle (calibration: BRAND, stays open; N1 rules only the sentences). That the home page's title carries no site name follows N1 and the Russian, German and Chinese titles. His remark is the first reader evidence on it and is recorded there.
As the first reader (observation 13): 'Begin the story' / «ابدأ الحكاية» is a button that scrolls to the next section and says so in neither source. Two readers now.
The sentence now says «“الاحساء” عربی لفظ “حسی” کی جمع ہے»: the sign he asks for, before the word. Vowel signs stay barred (P8 guard, P17). Ruled an explicitation, not an added fact (N7).

He calls it taste only, offers no wording, and each image is the sources' ('promising life', «تَعِد بالحياة»; 'story and rhythm', «حكايتها وإيقاعها»; 'capture the spirit of the place'; 'feel the oasis', 'the heritage heart'). «ارضیاتی عجوبہ» is ruled (P24) and is approved text. Heard by both readers and charged under nativeness; not rewritten in words nobody has read.

The line no longer says that everything is done by local hands: the date-picking stands free and the hands belong to the embroidery (stage 4's literal wording), and the garment is spelled as he reads it, «چوغوں» (with home.route.s2.d). The heading, round 1's «سرگرمیاں», he read as intended. That the line has no verb and does not say whether the visitor takes part is the source's.

As the first reader (observation 19): the source card names the dishes and explains none, and a gloss cannot stand in a card line. «ہریس» is the sourced form (the reference title; the Arabic is «الهريس»), and writing the dish he knows, «ہریسہ», would be a comparison the source does not make; «مفلق» stays pending for the food round.

Open item P3c. For labels it is ruled (P3c-labels): the name stands bare and the Urdu generic stands near it, here in the heading above («روایتی بازار»). He is the first reader to stop at «سوق»; the gloss form for running text stays open for batch b1, and his remark goes with it.

The two readers stopped at two different things in this slot: the first at «دن» under «پہلا دن» (one word for the day and for a part of it), the second at «دن میں» as no part of the day. What both miss is a part of the day, and the source does not give one: its label is 'Daytime' («النهار») between 'Morning' and 'Evening', and its line repeats 'by day'. «دوپہر», the first reader's word, would be a time the source does not carry. Round 1's wording stays: it removed the first confusion, which did not recur, and no reader passed the bare word. The change of register between the two days is the source's three labels (as the first reader, observation 24).

Both readers hear tale or legend in «داستان» beside early Islam (the first, observation 26). Their words, «تاریخ» and «واقعات», would turn 'one of the oldest stories in Islam' («واحدةً من أقدم حكايات الإسلام») into a statement about events: a change in how the site states its own claim, which is the owner's (P25). On record as a one-line option: «مٹی کی دیواریں، جو اسلام کے قدیم ترین واقعات میں سے ایک اپنے اندر سمیٹے ہوئے ہیں۔». Charged under fit. That the line does not say which story is the source's.
As the first reader (observation 31): 'story' five times in the English of the same five strings, «حكاية» in the Arabic, and the tagline is built on it.
As the first reader (observation 28): the day is headed 'Water and green' and begins at a mosque in both sources.

As the first reader (observation 27 a, b): the site rule keeps «الحساوي» inside this proper name and explains it nowhere, and the English name is as much a description. For the round that writes the farm's page (entry pending).

The dates now stand last, as in both sources. «ترشاوہ پھلوں» and «چنائی» stay: no wording was offered, both are the standard words (the dictionary gives «چنائی» for picking fruit), and the missing verb is the source's.

calibration.question: A quoted Arabic word that is letter for letter an Urdu word («حسی», the singular of the name, reads as the adjective 'sensory'): how is the reader told what he is looking at?
candidates: A — bare, inside quotation marks, after «لفظ» (stages 1 to 5) or with «لفظ» moved to the other name (round 1)
B — with its vowel signs, as the Arabic source writes it
C — with a language label: «عربی لفظ “حسی”»
calibration.evidence: Two blind readers, independently, read the adjective first and recovered only at the gloss that follows (round 1, observation 15; round 2, observation 15; moderate both times); the second reader names B and C as the remedies. A in both of its orders has therefore failed twice. B is barred: the P8 build guard rejects U+0650 and ruling P17 adds no vowel marks. C was weighed and declined at stage 3 as a fact neither source states. Against that reading: the sentence itself says the word is the singular of the name «الاحساء», an Arabic name, so that it is Arabic is contained in what is said; the Arabic source shows it to its reader by its script and its vowel signs, and the English by quoting a foreign word; the label is no measure, comparison or judgement (the test of ruling P28).
calibration.ruling_or_recommendation: C. «“الاحساء” عربی لفظ “حسی” کی جمع ہے، یعنی …». A language label on a quoted foreign word is an explicitation, not an added fact, when three things hold (the conditions of ruling P23): the label changes the form and not the content — the language is entailed by the sentence; the case is logged with the source observations and the literal wording recorded («“الاحساء” لفظ “حسی” کی جمع ہے»); and the labelled sentence is read blind. Vowel signs stay barred. The entry «حسی» stays pending until that reading.
calibration.binds: home.name.body; any later sentence that quotes an Arabic common word which unvocalised spells an Urdu word (the etymology of a name, a dish, a craft term).
calibration.guard: None mechanical. Proofreader: the label stands once, before the quoted word, and the word keeps its quotation marks.
